name: Epsilon Cygni
description: A giant of type K0 III 23.2 parsecs away, 12.4 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 197989: radius 12.41 +0.29/-0.3 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 4.985 +/- 0.046 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 197989: effective temperature 4659 +/- 35 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 197989: log g 2.67, from Allende Prieto & Lambert (1999), as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 4)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 197989: the Gaia DR2 (Gaia Collaboration 2018) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 43.18 +/- 0.94 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type K0 III, 23 parsecs away: 12.4 times the Sun's width and 65 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 4.985 milliarcseconds, which gives 12.41 solar radii and 4,659 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 197989: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1869302503206674304 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
